instruction: Can you tell me how to find the towing capacity of my vehicle?
chosen:
Yes, the towing capacity is rated by your vehicle manufacturer using a standardized rating system known as the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR). This includes the weight of your vehicle, any trailers and cargo, and any passengers and related gear. You’ll find the GVWR listed in the owner’s manual for most vehicles, and you can calculate the GVWR by subtracting the minimum allowable weight of the vehicle (called the Total Vehicle Empty Weight or TVEW) from the total unloaded vehicle weight as suggested by the manufacturer. The approximate formula is:

Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) = Total Unloaded Vehicle Weight - Minimum Total Vehicle Empty Weight

There are an infinite number of possible combinations of vehicle weight and trailer weight, so it’s important to check the GVWR rating of your current situation!

instruction: I have a general question. I was wondering if baking powder and baking soda the same thing?

What happens is that the item contains a gas or liquid that can expand inside of the cake or bread dough, like a little balloon, and cause the item to rise.  
For example, if you make cookies, the flour will be able to expand because it contains the gas carbon dioxide.  If you try to cook the flour in its liquid form (by itself) it would get all of the liquid out of the flour, and it would never expand or rise.  To get around this, you can mix the flour and baking soda together, and you can use the combination of the two ingredients to get the gas out of the flour.  Then, the gas from the baking soda can expand and lift the cookie.  Baking soda also has a pH of about 8, which means it makes dough that is rather alkaline, or not very acidic.  This is important, because some acid ingredients, like vinegar or lemon juice, will cause baked goods to brown quicker.

instruction: When and why does frostbite occur?
chosen:
When exposed to extremely cold temperatures, your body begins to lose heat.  This happens in two ways.  First, the cold air temperature causes heat loss through convection.  Your skin gets cold, and that cold skin radiates heat to the surrounding air.  Similarly, the air gets cold from contact with your skin, and it too emits heat to your skin.

The second way heat is lost is through radiation.  Cold air is a good radiator, and warm air is a good absorber.  As the air gets colder and the ground gets colder, your body heat radiates outward through the air into the ground, and vice versa.  This process can continue until you’re surrounded by cold air on all sides, and the heat loss from your body becomes extreme.
rejected: The skin can be injured by prolonged exposure to cold temperatures, or from the moisture in the cold air. Cold air is very drying, and can actually dry out the skin and tissue underneath. When this happens, you can get frostbite. Or, you can actually get frostbite when your skin gets cold and begins to freeze. This usually happens when you get too cold and your skin isn’t properly insulated. This also happens if you immerse your hand or foot in cold water for too long. In both situations, the cold air or water can cause the skin to freeze. This can cause injury if it occurs in enough of an area of the body, or it can cause pain if the tissue starts to freeze and thaw repeatedly.

instruction: What exactly causes volcanoes to form?
chosen:
From Wikipedia, “The development of volcanoes can be explained by the displacement of crustal plates. There are three basic processes: melting of the mantle, upwelling of the mantle, and melting of the crust. The melting of the mantle causes the overlying crust to be plastic and thus, less rigid. Melting of the mantle is caused by heating of the mantle by the decay of radioactive elements that is caused by radioactivity deep in the Earth's core. Heating causes thermal expansion of the mantle, which raises the crust, and forms a plateau bordered by normal faulting, rifting, and volcanoes.

A second process is upwelling of the mantle due to convection in the mantle. Convection is driven by a difference in density between the top and bottom of the mantle due to the influence of the overlying crust and plates. The third process is melting of the crust through rainwater and sea water. The most effective factor in producing volcanoes is the crustal movement. With enough thermal expansion, this will cause plates to separate from each other, with magma welling up at the plate boundary.”
rejected: Volcanic activity in the crust of the Earth takes place as part of the "Plate Tectonics" process.  During this process, pieces of the Earth's crust slide past each other, like pieces of a jigsaw puzzle, and sometimes friction in the plates can cause them to melt and form magma, which eventually causes volcanoes to erupt.  The formation of new volcanoes on the Earth is an ongoing process.

instruction: Can diabetes be reversed?
chosen: Yes, type 1 diabetes can be controlled through diet and insulin injections, but not reversed. Type 2 diabetes, or “adult-onset” diabetes, can be caused by lifestyle factors such as being overweight or obese, lack of exercise, and by heredity, and it can be reduced and controlled by a variety of methods, including dietary changes and weight loss. Type 2 diabetes is an autoimmune disease, so it cannot be fully “reversed”, but it can be reduced, and in some cases, people with type 2 diabetes can completely reverse it by having bariatric surgery to reduce their weight and reestablish normal gut microbiota.
rejected: It’s not that simple.  Diabetes is an abnormal function of your pancreas that causes it to make too much insulin.  If you could revert it to a normal level of insulin, that would be great.  Unfortunately this is quite difficult, because if you have too much insulin your body still doesn’t use the insulin well and therefore produces more insulin.  Diabetics are often prescribed insulin injections to try and reduce this effect.

instruction: How does a heart rate monitor detect the heart beats?
chosen: Well the concept is that there’s a special form of an electrocardiograph that can detect and display heart beats, through an electrode that’s attached to your chest. The electrode sends an electrical signal that represents your heart beats, and this is digitized through an Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC). The ADC also sends an electrical signal that represents the heart beats, which is displayed on the monitor.
rejected: A pulse oximeter measures the amount of blood the heart pumps in and out.  This indicates the rate at which the heart is beating.  A monitor sends a constant amount of red and infrared light through your finger or earlobe.  When the light is absorbed by the blood flowing through the heart, it’s reflected by your body’s hemoglobin.  The amount of light absorbed and reflected changes depending on the heartbeat.  A monitor uses these light fluctuations to calculate your heart rate.

instruction: How does carbon dating work?
chosen: Carbon dating is a radiometric dating technique that uses mathematical calculations to measure the decay rate of a specific radioactive isotope of carbon, specifically carbon-14 (14C) to estimate the age of carbonaceous materials up to about 60,000 years old.  Carbon-14 is a radioactive isotope of carbon with a radioactive half-life of about 6020 years. The ratio of carbon-14 to the stable carbon isotope, carbon-12, in a sample can be compared to the current ratio in the environment, which is known from measurements, to estimate when the sample was last in equilibrium with the environment.
rejected: Carbon dating is a method of determining the age of an object containing carbon on the basis of measurable amounts of carbon-14 in the object, and the known rate of decay of this radioisotope. The method was developed in the late 1940s, and is based on the properties of radioactive decay of carbon-14 into nitrogen, with a half-life of around 6,000 years. Carbon dating analysis is done on items up to 50,000 years old, which relies on a mathematical plot that extrapolates the data to estimate the date. Carbon dating is useful for assigning approximate dates to many kinds of archeological artifacts, as well as bone, cloth, and paper objects produced by humans that have been saved over long periods of time. For carbon dating to be accurate, the ratio of carbon-14 to stable carbon-12 in the object being measured must remain consistent with the ratio in the atmosphere, and the measurement analysis must correct for several potential sources of error to produce reliable dating results.

instruction: How does our immune system fight viruses?
chosen:
Your immune system helps keep you healthy and safe from disease by recognizing and responding to foreign substances in the body called antigens. This allows the body to deactivate or get rid of antigens and infection.

One way your body does this is through white blood cells (also called leukocytes), which are highly specialized cells that serve as the backbone of your immune system. A leukocyte called a phagocyte will swallow or engulf an infectious agent like a virus. If it is only weakly resistant to the phagocyte, it will simply be broken down or degraded and destroyed. A stronger infectious agent will engulf the phagocyte in return and cause it to produce proteases or substances that help the body’s immune system fight the infection.

After engulfing an antigen, phagocytes will release chemical signals to activate the immune system, which makes other immune cells produce cytokines and chemokines that can trigger rapid inflammation in the body. Other immune system cells, such as B cells and T cells, can also help fight infections if properly instructed.

Our immune system creates antibodies and other immune cells called lymphocytes in order to detect cells or other foreign substances in the body that don’t belong there. Some of the antibodies produced by the immune system can even neutralize a virus by
rejected: Well, our body’s “immune system” is really a group of systems that work together to protect us against harmful substances such as bacteria and viruses.  There are several ways that our immune system helps fight off invaders, including increased heart rate, sweating, and inflammation.  In the case of viruses, our body first build up antibodies against them, which block the virus from entering new cells in our body.  Sometimes, the virus will be able to slip past the antibodies, and to kill cells in the human body, which is really harmful.  Many viruses will be successfully fought by our immune system, though, so we often have mild or even no symptoms from a viral infection at all.

instruction: I would like to know the difference between was is considered fact and reasoned judgment
chosen:
Well, facts are things like “the Sun rises in the East” or “if I have 10 apples, then I have more than 5 apples” that are true no matter what time of day or year it is.

So if you believe something is true, it’s a fact. But in science and logic we like to get it right in a way that’s “reasoned” or “rational”, where you have good reasons to think something is true, and you don’t just believe it for no good reason. 
For example, I might say “I believe that apples are round.” But I could have a few reasons to think that -- because my friend once ate one that was round, or because I once tried to drop one on my head and it seemed to get a small bump instead of a big dent, etc.
rejected: A reasoned judgment is a logical deduction from facts, based on a premise that is itself an assumption.  “The sun is in the sky” is a factual statement, while “The earth is round” is an assumption.  A factual statement may or may not be true, but an assumption is always true unless proven otherwise.

instruction: I'm doing a research project about badgers. Can you give me some info about them?
chosen: Sure, badgers are small to medium-sized mammals found primarily in Europe and western Asia, although there are also populations in northwest Africa and various parts of North America.  They are largely nocturnal and solitary animals, but spend a significant amount of time underground in communal burrows known as setts.  Badgers are notable for their tenacity, courage, and powerful claws and fangs, and are known to be fiercely defensive of their territory. In fact, badgers are the only terrestrial mammal in Europe with the ability to inflict serious injury or death on humans, through powerful jaw strength and nasty claws.  Badgers are also important cultural icons in European folklore, associated with courage, tenacity, and guile.  Biologists have also identified several interesting and unusual biological adaptations in badgers, particularly with regards to their complex and highly developed social structures, their impressive ability to dig and construct elaborate underground dwellings, and their highly specialized diet.
rejected: Badgers are medium-sized mammals, belonging to the species Mustelidae, which also includes several other similarly-sized species, such as otters and weasels.  Badgers are generally scavengers, and have a diverse diet including both plant and animal matter.  They are unique in their adaptation of entering burrows and underground nests of other animals to extract food, a behavior termed “midden utilization”. Badgers are generally solitary and nocturnal creatures.  Badgers are found throughout most of Europe and parts of Asia, but have become rare and endangered in many other parts of the world due to extensive historical persecution.  Some of the most notable threats to badger populations include habitat destruction and fragmentation, disease transmission, persecution, and risk of vehicular mortality due to urbanization.

instruction: How do you get rid of drain flies?
chosen:
Drain flies are a type of fly that live in water draining from your kitchen sink, bathtub, or other sink basin or hot water tap. They can be an annoyance, but they don’t usually do any harm. There are a few effective ways to prevent drain flies:
-Open the kitchen window each morning while you’re cooking, use a fan, or use an exhaust hood over the sink. The flies will be discouraged from entering your home, as the exterior provides more comfortable conditions for them to thrive. If you have a bathroom window or vent, try opening it while you shower to allow fresh air to circulate.
-Open the kitchen window each night to allow the entire house to air out while you sleep. Drain flies dislike very dry environments, and prefer to lay their eggs in humid conditions.
-Shower regularly to prevent the need for drain flies to enter your home. If you have a bathroom window or vent, try opening it while you shower to allow fresh air to circulate.
-Drain plungers and traps can be used in the sinks and bathrooms to prevent drain flies from breeding and laying eggs.
-Run your dishwasher and washing machine regularly to heat up your kitchen and bathroom. Drain flies
rejected: Cold temperatures are often effective in killing off drain flies, but in addition you can use various chemical pesticides to get rid of drain flies.  If you are especially concerned about chemical residues in your household, you can also try vacuuming the flies out of the drain, or using common household vinegar to drown the flies.

instruction: Can you explain how the SWIFT financial system works?
chosen: The Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT) is a bank consortium that serves as a secure communication network for banks and financial institutions all around the world.  SWIFT facilitates and streamlines secure banking transactions, and the communication network provided by SWIFT allows confidential and secure messaging between financial institutions and customers.  SWIFT is a secure means of transferring messages and funding across international borders, and most international financial activity is conducted through the network offered by SWIFT.  SWIFT is a non-profit organization and serves member institutions worldwide, including tens of thousands of banks, credit unions, corporations, and government organizations. SWIFT is headquartered in Belgium’s European Union capital Brussels, and it serves over 11,000 member organizations in more than 200 countries.
rejected:
Sure! The SWIFT financial system is a secure global network for payment transactions understood as standardized messages using a common language. Integrating over 12,000 financial institutions in over 200 countries, SWIFT provides a unprecedented level of protection and reliability for international payments worldwide.  The messages are secure, automated, and guaranteed globally shared standards using “know your customer” procedures to prevent fraud and errors by any participants, eliminating the need for parties to transact in multiple differing locations or systems to clear and settle cross-border payments. Creation, usage, processing, and delivery of these secure messages is governed by International Banking and Finance Association (IBA) Rules, SWIFT’s local based rules, and general laws and regulations.  

Messages and associated funds move through the SWIFT payment system via several supervisory functions:

1) The issuing bank (is considered the sender, originator, or submitter of a payment order, i.e. the payer).  

2) The national operating center where the payments system of the issuer is based guidelines the processing and clearing functions of the payment order.  The national operating center verifies information (a mandatory part of this is verifying the passport details of the appointed payer) and sends the payment order to another national operating center that is connected to the domestic clearing system of the payee, including the identification and authentication of the payer, to authorize the payment. 

3) Depositary bank is a receiving bank where deposited funds are available.  After the payment order is sent by a national operating center to the depositary bank associated with the payee’s domestic clearing system, which records the transaction after authorization by the local authorization entities.

Please note that SWIFT handles multiple asset types for payment, including foreign currencies, foreign currency forward contracts, securities transactions, transferable deposits, bank guarantees, fund-transfer letters of credit, and local Area Payments System funds transfers.  

The SWIFT payment system supports these functions through a network connection between banks, strongly-interconnected national payment switching centers, and administration services that ensure network users are known and verified.   The SWIFT payment system is coordinated and supervised by SWIFT’s governing bodies: the SWIFT Governing Council and the management team at SWIFT.

SWIFT Corporate

instruction: How do I prune roses?
chosen:
Roses are lovely flowering plants.  
When you prune roses, you remove the “dead wood” and dead flowers, to let the plant produce flowers with longer, better stems.  Pruning helps the plant to become more beautiful and to grow better over time.  
The roses you buy in a store are cut from their original plant, so you’ll have to wait a while before you see the results of pruning.  You can cut roses with pruning shears or a pruning saw.  
To prune a rose bush, start by holding the pruned end of the stem with your free hand.  Cut where you want to cut with the pruning saw.  If you cut directly across the stem, you’ll cut off all the flowers and new growth.  Make a “V” cut so you cut off new growth but keep the stems with flowers attached.  If you cut too deeply, the stem will grow out again and you’ll need to start over.  
When you’re done, cover the wound with a bandage.  Make a fresh cut next year to induce a flush of growth.  

You’ll want to re-prune roses every few years, to get them to produce lots of flower buds.

You could also remove leaves that are partially eaten by pests, or pruning away damaged leaves can increase the number of flowers.  When you’re done pruning, make sure that the water reservoir is full, and water the plant regularly.

instruction: How do I change the oil in my 1965 gmc truck

- A screwdriver or hex wrench to open the oil drain plug
- A funnel to drain the oil

Next, gently tighten the drain plug using a wrench, and then replace the oil filter and torque the filter to 22ft-lb.  Start the engine and let it run for 30 minutes. Pagsamba:

instruction: How can I convince the airline to let me take my dog in the cabin of the plane?

Here are some general strategies that might help you to convince the airline to allow your dog to fly in the cabin with you:  

-Use a reputable service dog organization certification. Airlines generally prefer this type of certification because it is an independent third-party assessment of the dog’s suitability for the program.
-Provide documentation from your veterinarian that your dog has no health or behavior issues that would make it a disruption or danger to other passengers.
-Explain how your dog is a vital support for you and your disability, and explain how you will need your dog’s assistance during the flight (for example, if you are disabled and rely on your dog for mobility assistance).
-If your dog is well-behaved, you may want to provide documentation or evidence of this. You could try bringing a photo of your dog sitting quietly and calmly.
-Be patient with the airline reservation staff. Explain calmly and rationally why you think your dog should be allowed to fly with you, and ask them to assist you in getting this approved. If they are unable to help you, ask them to transfer you to a supervisor or department that may be able to help.
-If all else fails, consider flying on another airline or travelling at a different time of year (when there may be less demand for cabin space). You could also consider taking an alternate flight that is not as critical, so that you have more flexibility regarding your travel arrangements.

instruction: Can you explain how GPS works?
chosen: Sure.  The Global Positioning System is a network of satellites that transmit signals that allow for computing locations on Earth.  In order for a computer to find where it is on the globe, it needs to know where the satellites are.  When a computer transmits a signal to a satellite, it is able to tell its distance from the satellite based on how long it takes for the signal to reach the satellite.  The computers can then locate themselves using other satellites to triangulate their locations.

It does this by using signals sent by satellites orbiting the earth.  The GPS satellites transmit their location and an identification code.  Every GPS receiver has a GPS antenna that can “listen” for these signals.  Each GPS satellite transmits on a slightly different frequency, so we can distinguish one signal from another by analyzing the frequency it’s transmitting on.  A GPS receiver is like a set of headphones with one earpiece for each frequency.  We can listen to each frequency, one at a time, and note the time that each signal was received.  This will give us the exact time of transmission for each satellite.  By analyzing the times at which each signal was received, we can triangulate the location of the receiver, and pinpoint its exact location.  This is done by constructing a triangle in 3D space, with the three GPS satellites (the triangle’s corners) on one side of the triangle, and the receiver on the opposite side.  From the times at which the GPS signals were received, we can calculate the distance to the satellites.

instruction: What are humors? And I don't mean joke-humor, it's some outdated medical theory.

Humor theory says that there are four “elements” in the human body: fire, earth, air, and water. Different people were said to have an excess of one of those elements, and this resulted in different physical characteristics and personality traits. You might hear phrases like “choleric” or “melancholic”, which were used to describe the personality traits associated with a certain humor. rejected: Humors were a classical theory of medicine dating back to ancient Greece.  The theory proposed that human health and personality are determined by a blend of four essential fluids or “humors” which needed to be kept in proper balance in order to maintain health.  These humors were identified as blood, yellow bile, black bile, and phlegm.  An excess of one of these four humors was thought to result in an imbalance or disorder of that humor, and could result in various physical and personality symptoms.  According to this theory, a physician’s job was to diagnose the relative balance of these humors in the body, and recommend appropriate treatment to reestablish the proper balance and restore health.  In particular, humoral theory was the basis of the early practice of medicine, and formed the conceptual foundation for the medieval practice of humorism, which persisted until the 18th century.  While modern medicine has abandoned humoral theory, it remains relevant as a historical example of how prevailing theories and beliefs can affect our understanding and comprehension of human physiology and health.

instruction: Why does butter explode in the microwave?
chosen: Butter is made of triglycerides, which are fats. And fats can change into a different molecular structure called a fat crystal, which is more stable and has a different shape. When the microwave energy heats the butter to a higher temperature, the fat molecules get jostled and become more likely to align into fat crystals. The fat molecules tend to arrange in a spherical crystal lattice, which means the crystals will have relatively high surface area and tend to lose energy by dissipating heat rapidly. When a fat crystal absorbs energy, it can heat up so fast that its surface tension can’t keep it from exploding. That’s what makes the butter bubbles rise up and pop in the microwave.
rejected: It’s not really that butter “explodes”, it’s just that when the butter melts, it becomes less concentrated, which causes the liquid to expand into a gas.  You see this same thing happen when you add a bunch of salt to water, which results in the “fizz” of a sparkling water drink.  You might say that butter “explodes” in the microwave, but it’s the expansion of the liquid in the microwave that is responsible for the splashing.

instruction: What are the differences between regular yogurt and Greek yogurt?

Greek yogurt is much thicker and creamier than regular yogurt, and has a higher protein content. Most Greek yogurts have a 3-5% fat content, while most regular yogurts are only around 2% fat. In addition, most Greek yogurts are strained longer so as to remove almost all of the lactose and sugars, resulting in a high protein and low sugar yogurt. Finally, Greek yogurts generally have a much thicker and sharper yogurt “bite,” and have a slightly higher salt content. Regular yogurt is available in many delicious varieties and flavors, but Greek yogurt has a more limited, yet delicious, array of offerings including vanilla and plain. 

----

While Greek yogurt is richer and more dense, it still retains the probiotic bacteria of regular yogurt, providing health benefits including better bowel health and improved immune function. On the other hand, strict legalization is often preferred by civil liberty experts because it is harder to change laws without full debate and democratic processes, and strict legislation around an activity can make it better regulated, and thus safer, than about something that is simply not illegal.
